intent: Revert wheel_track to 0.10 m, the setting that gave 20 of 20 oval finishes and the best s-bend progress (0.42), because iteration 7's oval collapse followed the narrower 0.09 m track. Keep the widened five-sensor row at x=±0.07, y=0.08, with 12 mm footprints, since it removed the slalom line losses in iteration 7. Hold body, wheels and mass unchanged. Expected: oval finish rate at least 0.85, slalom line_loss_events near 0 with progress above 0.12, and s-bend progress at or above 0.42.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that wheel_track 0.09 with the ±0.07 row broke the oval (finish 0.15) and the s-bend (progress 0.18), while the ±0.07 row removed slalom line losses (1.0 to 0.0). Iteration 5 showed wheel_track 0.10 with ±0.06 is stable on the oval. This race tests whether the ±0.07 row is compatible with the 0.10 track. If the oval finish stays at or above 0.85 and slalom losses stay at 0, the row widening is confirmed and the next lever is the s-bend turn rate with the track held at 0.10. If the oval still fails with the 0.10 track, the widened row is the cause, and the next step is to return to ±0.06 and address the slalom through controller base_speed or weights rather than sensing. Ask the Integrator whether slalom line losses are gone and where the slalom off-track exit now happens.
rationale:
Iteration 7 scored 122.83, the second-worst result, and the evidence shows which change caused it. Oval finish fell from 1.0 (iteration 5) to 0.15, with 17 off-track exits and progress 0.38. Steering oscillation on the oval was low at 0.122, so the failure is not jitter. The s-bend also got worse, with progress falling from 0.42 to 0.18 and max_error at 0.065. On the slalom, line losses fell from 1.0 to 0.0 per run, which supports the wider row x=±0.07. The slalom still went off track at progress 0.12 with max_error 0.0636, so the wider row helped sensing but did not complete the course.

Iteration 7 changed two geometry variables at once: wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m and the row x=±0.06 to ±0.07. The oval collapse and the s-bend regression point at the narrower track. A 0.09 m track gives about 11 percent more yaw per unit of steering command, and the oval finish rate already fell to 0.85 when extra authority was added in iteration 4. The Robot Integrator's decision rule (oval finish below 0.85 means return wheel_track to 0.10 and keep the row change) applies directly. I follow it.

For iteration 8, I set wheel_track back to 0.10 m, the best-scoring track so far, and keep the widened row x=±0.07 at y=0.08 with 12 mm footprints. The row is the one change that removed slalom line losses, so keeping it isolates whether the oval collapse came from the track. Body, wheels, mass and sensor size stay as in iteration 5. The off-track floor still binds at 0.06 m for every body width, so body changes are not useful here.

Expected result: oval finish back to at least 0.85 (ideally 1.0), slalom line_loss_events near 0 with slalom progress above 0.12, and s-bend progress at or above 0.42. The main risk is that the wider row alone reduces oval stability, which the measurements below will show.
